purpose: Structured FTC Cleo AI refund ledger distinguishing an announced aggregate PayPal distribution from delivery, acceptance, adequacy, and later household outcomes.

events.geography: United States; consumers who paid Cleo AI for eligible instant cash advances
events.date_precision: Day precision for FTC announcement; payment sending begins 2026-10-27 and email notification window runs 2026-10-08 through 2026-10-26
events.denominator: 2,124,796 planned PayPal payments; aggregate eligible-recipient count, not a retained person-level denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official FTC refund page, press release, and case page
events.missingness: No recipient identifiers, individual payment amount, notification receipt, delivery success, acceptance, return, subscription/account correction, original loss, household budget effect, repeat borrowing, trust, switching, or exit are retained
events.exposure: The FTC alleged Cleo AI misled consumers about the amount and timing of cash advances, charged additional express fees, and made subscription cancellation difficult
events.alternatives_before_action: Consumers could seek cancellation, dispute or refund routes, use other credit or payment sources, delay a need, or continue using the service; person-level feasible alternatives and borrowing substitution are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Consumers faced alleged delayed or smaller-than-promised advances, express fees, subscription friction, and potential cash-flow strain; the public record does not quantify individual loss or household incidence
events.choice_or_response: The FTC announced payments by PayPal, email notification before the distribution date, and a 30-day acceptance window; individual notification, delivery, acceptance, rejection, or return is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: FTC and refund administrator control eligibility and distribution; PayPal controls delivery and acceptance mechanics; consumers control acceptance within the stated window under unknown account and liquidity constraints
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The FTC announced more than $15.8 million in 2,124,796 PayPal payments, beginning 2026-10-27, after a $17 million settlement; the public announcement provides a refund-administrator route and warns against impersonation scams
events.remedy_receipt: Aggregate payments are announced but no recipient-level delivery, acceptance, or receipt is verified
events.durability_followup: No later account correction, subscription cancellation, repeat borrowing, household recovery, trust, switching, or exit record is public in the announcement packet
events.immediate_outcome: A large-scale consumer-redress route is announced with a dated future delivery start and a bounded acceptance window
events.protected_outcome: A payment may return part of the alleged financial harm to eligible consumers, but amount adequacy and usable receipt are not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Delayed cash, express fees, subscription burden, effort, and residual loss remain unmeasured at consumer level
events.cost_risk_transfer: The refund route shifts some financial responsibility toward the firm and administrator, while delivery, acceptance, account access, and residual-loss risk remain with consumers until receipt is established
events.later_outcome: The route is not yet an observed payment outcome at the 2026-10-19 checkpoint; delivery, acceptance, return, adequacy, financial recovery, repeat borrowing, trust, switching, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: The agency attributes alleged deceptive cash-advance and subscription practices to Cleo AI, but consumer-level fairness, trust, blame, or legitimacy change is not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: FTC enforcement and refund administration are observed; consumer organizing, complaint persistence, and political action are not linked
events.counterexample: A planned aggregate PayPal distribution can coexist with failed delivery, unaccepted payment, account access friction, inadequate amount, or continued financial dependence
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official FTC refund page (https://search.ftc.gov/enforcement/refunds/cleo-ai-refunds), FTC press release dated 2026-10-08 (https://search.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/10/ftc-returns-more-158-million-consumers-misled-cash-advance-app-company-cleo-ai), and FTC case page (https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/cases-proceedings/cleo-ai-inc-ftc-v). The public records establish the planned aggregate distribution and dates, not individual delivery, acceptance, adequacy, account correction, or later household outcome

arrows.from: alleged deceptive cash-advance and subscription practices
arrows.evidence: The FTC case page and press release describe the allegations, $17 million settlement, and refund program
arrows.counterexample: The enforcement record does not identify every affected consumer or quantify each person's loss
arrows.remaining_gap: Consumer-level exposure, loss, fees, cancellation effort, and eligibility

arrows.evidence: The FTC says eligible consumers will receive email notification between October 8 and October 26, with PayPal payments beginning October 27, 2026
arrows.counterexample: Notification, payment initiation, and successful delivery are separate events and may fail at different stages
arrows.remaining_gap: Recipient identity, notification receipt, delivery success, bounced or returned payments, and timing

arrows.evidence: The FTC instructs recipients to accept the payment within 30 days, but the public announcement reports no acceptance or return outcomes
arrows.counterexample: A delivered payment can remain unaccepted, be returned, or be inaccessible because of account or identity friction
arrows.remaining_gap: Acceptance, return, account access, identity resolution, and payment date

arrows.to: financial recovery, continued borrowing, trust, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The FTC refund and case pages provide no recipient-level later household, borrowing, trust, or behavior follow-up
arrows.counterexample: Receiving a refund does not establish adequacy, restored liquidity, cancellation, or changed reliance on cash-advance products
arrows.remaining_gap: Individual amount, original loss, adequacy, household recovery, repeat borrowing, trust, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger establishes a dated official consumer-redress offer with a planned aggregate payment and explicit future acceptance window. It does not establish recipient-level delivery, receipt, adequate recovery, account correction, trust, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only compact official page-derived fields and source URLs are retained; no recipient identifiers, PayPal data, payment file, or raw personal data is downloaded.
